paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—on the MMLU dataset. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," ranges from 0.86 to 1.00, representing the model's initial confidence in its predictions, and is scaled linearly with tick marks at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," measures the accuracy of predictions, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale. The blue line, representing Final Accuracy, starts at approximately 0.92 when initial confidence is 0.86 and remains relatively stable, fluctuating slightly around 0.95–0.98 before ending at 0.97. The green line, representing Initial Accuracy, begins at 0.65 and steadily increases to a peak of 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.96, then declines slightly to 0.78 at the highest confidence level. The orange line, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at 0.28 and decreases to 0.0 at an initial confidence of 0.93, then rises again to 0.22 at the highest confidence level. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
